The *Bhallātadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha Ap 446) is a canonical verse text situated within the Therāpadāna section of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text belongs to the collection of biographical narratives recounting the past karmic actions and spiritual careers of Buddhist elders. SuttaCentral lists five modern translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].

Text-reuse calculations by DharmaNexus show that the poem is composed with standard formulaic structures typical of the collection, sharing 110 matching passages across 43 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. A major segment spanning §1.1–6.3 is closely aligned with the commentary on the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Dutiyo bhāgo, §860–871), with additional recurrent phrases matched in the first volume of that commentary [DharmaNexus]. Within the Therāpadāna itself, the closing segments (§6.1/§6.2–11.1) exhibit substantial textual identity with formulaic verses in other fruit-offering poems, such as the *Pilakkhaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 386), *Ajeliphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 509), *Mātuluṅgaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 508), *Vallikāraphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 480), and *Piyālaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 502) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-linguistic matches identified by DharmaNexus include low-scoring machine alignments with Tibetan canonical texts, such as the *Vinayavastu* (D0001-2) and D0343, though these reflect common formulaic wording rather than established textual parallels [DharmaNexus].
